gen-dafont-early-gameboy-plus-jakarta-sa: Playful and commanding, Early GameBoy stretches its letters wide and towers with a skyward x-height. And Plus Jakarta Sans is its tidy opposite, a monoline sans-serif that keeps its curve endings well apart.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-amulya: Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals, every stroke held to a single constant width. Amulya follows in a plain sans with generous gaps in its curves, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-chillax: Lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals defines Edo SZ, while Chillax loops along like spaghetti laid out in letters. Shrink the heading and that heft fades.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-plein: Edo SZ stands out for lowercase letters as tall as cast iron capitals, drawn with a line that never swells or tapers. Plein feeds a clear channel into each round letter.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads approachably, with wide gaps between curve ends and stems and strokes of identical weight in both directions. Edo SZ supplies the towering, cast iron lowercase above it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-synonym: Dependable is the word for Synonym, a sans with a plain stripe of constant ink and generous openings in every curve, under the heading Edo SZ. Edo SZ makes the statement; Synonym carries the text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-bree-serif: Heavy, rounded and sure of itself, Edo SZ keeps every bowl outline the same all the way around. Bree Serif then offers a classic serif with outsized lowercase proportions, which makes extended reading feel literary.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-quando: Edo SZ looks like ink poured at a single width, with cast iron stature. Quando sits beneath with sparse, wide spacing and a big, tall middle zone, so give its lines generous room.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-outfit: Classic in its cast iron lowercase, Edo SZ keeps one constant stroke width throughout. And Outfit bends cable-like curves that finish well before they close, so a larger body size suits it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-plus-jakarta-sans: A lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, all at one constant stroke width, makes Edo SZ unmistakable. But Plus Jakarta Sans is the precise one, a monoline sans-serif keeping its curve endings well apart.
